attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his signed post, not a quote of someone else.

semantics.note: A faithful restatement of an unhedged present-tense observation contrasting formal verification in math with other domains.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. 'Straightforward' means mechanically checking a formal proof, not finding it, and 'elsewhere' takes its meaning from the surrounding open-ended examples (medicine, robotics). That reading is neither stretched for nor against him. The result does depend on that reading.

evidence.note: Dated 2026-11-21, within the target period. A primary verification record showing compilation, statement comparison and independent kernel checks. It comes from the Lean and Mathlib maintainers, so it is partly self-reporting, but it describes checks by several independent checkers.

A technical abstract for a talk dated Nov 17. It says guarantees for autonomous systems hold only if the model captures uncertainty, which is a substantial modelling obstacle. It also notes that guarantees are possible within models, so it qualifies the claim without meeting the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: Under the plain reading, e1 shows that the formal Lean proof was checked mechanically by several independent checkers. e2 shows that guarantees for open-ended empirical systems such as robots require substantial modelling of uncertainty. Both parts of the support condition are met. No evidence shows comparable guarantees without extra modelling work. This is not a numerical comparison across every domain.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed post.

semantics.note: Two parts: the proof relied heavily on Lean and mathlib, and comparable resources are absent in a field like medicine. The normalisation keeps both.

contract.note: Reading 'comparable' as a broadly reusable formal knowledge library plus a verification system, rather than any medical database, is a fair, ordinary reading. It does not require medicine to have no formal methods at all.

evidence.note: The Lean FRO and Mathlib joint statement shows the codebase depends directly only on Mathlib and was verified in Lean. It is labelled an independent measurement but is the maintainers' own statement. It supports the dependence part only.
A 2008 demonstration of theorem proving on one diabetes guideline. It is from a different period and is narrow, so it cannot show whether comparable medical infrastructure existed in November 2026.

reviews.rationale: e5 establishes heavy dependence on Mathlib and Lean. Nothing in the packet establishes whether medicine had a comparable formal library and verification infrastructure as of the post date, and the packet itself says no inventory was found. e6 is old and narrow. The comparison part, which is central to the claim, is unsettled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his signed post.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps the evaluative parts (usefulness, elegance), the 250,000-page figure, the 'yet' on general lessons, and the 'so far as I have heard' qualifier on new techniques.

contract.note: It is charitable to read 250,000 pages as the generated exposition rather than the released Lean proof. Scoring 'no new techniques' against the public record partly sets aside his 'so far as I have heard', but the contract says so openly. An informed reader takes a public commentator to be asserting that none had been identified. Usefulness and elegance are not scored.

evidence.note: Alpöge's footnote says a generated document reached 250,000+ pages. That supports the approximate figure, though the document was not released and was not independently counted.

A dated Nov 21 outline, published before the post, calls a specific tower construction apparently new. It meets the contract's public-record contradiction condition, though it is provisional and AI-assisted.

reviews.rationale: The page-count part holds: e3 supports roughly 250,000+ pages for the generated exposition. The novelty part is contradicted on the public-record reading: e4 identified an apparently new construction before the post, although Marcus limited this to what he had heard. 'No general lessons yet' is not settled by the packet. Usefulness and elegance are evaluative and not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion that the result was not AI alone.

semantics.note: The checkable part is 'not the case' that AI alone solved it. The claim about social-media beliefs is fairly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'alone' as excluding substantive human mathematical collaboration is the ordinary reading.

evidence.note: A participant account from Alpöge, not Marcus. He describes guiding the approach and formalizing the argument together with Claude, which shows substantive human mathematical participation. He is an interested party, but this is the source type the contract prefers.

reviews.rationale: Alpöge's own account (e1) describes him directing the mathematical approach and formalizing the proof jointly with Claude. That meets the support condition of substantive human participation. The packet has no development record showing an autonomous AI proof. How much each side contributed cannot be measured, but that is not needed to score the claim.
